prompt: Support finds past tickets with similar meaning even when they use different words.
tells: similar meaning even when they use different words
why: Embeddings turn text into numbers where similar meanings sit close, so matching works without shared words.
trap: Grounding uses what's found; finding it by meaning is embeddings.

prompt: Each product description is turned into a list of 1,536 numbers.
why: A list of numbers that captures meaning is an embedding, also called a vector.
trap: Tokens are text pieces; this is a numeric representation of meaning.

prompt: The app recommends songs whose lyric vectors are nearest to the one you liked.
why: Nearness between vectors stands for similar meaning. Recommending by nearest vector uses embeddings.
trap: No tool is being called; the match is made with vectors.

prompt: A search for 'cheap car' also finds a page about 'affordable vehicles'.
tells: also finds a page about 'affordable vehicles'
why: The words differ but the meanings are close, so their embeddings are close too. That's search by meaning.
trap: Nothing was rephrased; the search compared meanings.

prompt: Thousands of survey comments are grouped by meaning so themes show up.
why: Comments with close embeddings fall into the same group. Grouping by meaning uses embeddings.
trap: No answer is being written from sources; the texts are compared as vectors.

prompt: The team stores document vectors in a database so they can find the closest ones fast.
why: A vector database keeps embeddings so similar items can be looked up quickly.
trap: It may feed a tool or a prompt, but the stored vectors are embeddings.
